defects.detail: ཉན་པའི་དབང་ནི་མནོས་པས། གསང་སྔགས་རྒྱུད་ཆེན་མཉན་པ་རྣམས rendered 'received the power of hearing but listen ... with faults' — 'with faults' has no counterpart
opening གཞུང་ཉམས་བྱེད (damages the scripture) rendered as editorial 'The text continues the degeneration of the teachings'
ད་ཡང་འདུས་པའི་སྙིང་པོ་ཉོན (listen to the essence of the Compendium) rendered as vocative 'listen, Heart of the Assembly!'

reason: Simile-by-simile the samaya-breach verses track the source (tongue-ploughed hell, hell of mutes, hot and dark hells, boat/eyes similes, Mahayoga confession); small added 'with faults' and a vocative reading of 'essence of the Düpa'; my Tibetan reading is moderate.
Modernised English faithfully renders the sentencing clauses, the order of examination 'a part', and questions 1–2; the note on 'the third' is interpretive, not invention.

defects.detail: 子夏曰微悁而勇若悁者可乎 (without Yuan, one as brave as Yuan — acceptable?) rendered 'one who is irritable like him'
陸龜蒙詩佳哉鹿門子好問如丨丨 merged with next headword 虎豹痟 into 'fond of asking questions as if tiger or leopard aches'
列子 quote: ——體煩內熱 (the dashes stand for headword 心痟) dropped; 增嬰痟 rendered vaguely as 'Added: To suffer from an ache'
痟 entry with 烏玄切 glossed '(xiāo) wasting disease' though the fanqie gives yuan; 鹿門子 rendered 'Master of Lumen'

reason: Peiwen yunfu-style entries for 悁/𤸎 are mostly recognisable, but the Han Shi waizhuan punchline (勇若悁 'as brave as Yuan') is mistranslated, and the Lu Guimeng / 虎豹 entries are run together into fluent nonsense.

defects.detail: 'Mobilicia pat' rendered 'Mauricia Pat'
'ca mal kal tun' rendered 'forty k'aan' with a gloss 'linear land measures of about twenty meters' not in the source

the boundary survey 'llobu tun tu noh bel Sotol ... tu nix bu tun ... ox ho ... nil tan kan cab' rendered as a confident survey with 'sunset (west)', 'north', 'right-hand side', 'flat red earth' that the garbled source does not clearly support
'ten Juana Dzul cimic glegorio pat' (cimic likely 'deceased') treated as a verb 'sell'

reason: Stamp text and the sale formula (Gregorio Pat, two pesos, seven tumin each) are rendered plausibly, but the uncertain Maya of the boundary description is turned into fluent, specific directions; I read colonial Yucatec weakly.

reason: Latin headnotes and the Italian letter of Pandolfini (plague transfer, papal brief, 1 March 1478) and notes 59–60 rendered completely and accurately.
German Weigel citations and the Latin connective (truncum transmutationem, hydra, Delubra ad sacra Draconem) and the Paracelsus quotation rendered fully and accurately; notes are interpretive.
Ptolemy's epicycle construction (117;37,32 / 120 / 631;13,48, apogee Λ, perigee M, Eucl. III 36) rendered accurately; ends where source ends.

reason: Dalberg's titles and the medal/invitation sentence are faithful; the final clause is completed with content from beyond the page.

defects.detail: ཡེ་ཤེས་ལས་མ་སྐྱེས་པ་དང་ (not born from the wisdom) rendered 'not unborn from the self-knowing wisdom', a double negative that reverses the sense
opening fragment ཆེན་པོ་ (end of a prior phrase) rendered as vocative 'Great Being'

reason: Chapter colophons 8 and 9, the 'marvelous secret' reasons and the five-bodies play passage are faithfully rendered; one double-negative slip and the OCR's གཉིད (sleep) passed through with a note.

defects.detail: Lion-ram-lotus 'source 9/6' rendered '9/16'
Gryphon in Abydos '12/16/21' rendered '12/21' (16 dropped)
source 'Yaes', 'Yarmeich', 'Zalabaho', 'Lion comes', 'Pessiwont' rendered 'Yaeo', 'Yarmeeh', 'Zalabahs', 'Loou comes', 'Perriwont'
'dem. gl. 191' rendered '<note>Demotic equivalent</note> ql. 191'

reason: English index reproduced nearly entirely, but several names and two reference numbers differ from the source text (some match the image, 'Perriwont' and '9/16' match neither).
image_note: Image reads 'Yaeo' (OCR 'Yaes'), 'Loou comes' (OCR 'Lion comes'), 'Zalabahs' (OCR 'Zalabaho'), 'Gryphon in Abydos 12/21 with 16 superscript' (OCR '12/<gloss>16</gloss>/21').

reason: Iconography (implements of four right and four left hands, five skulls, Akshobhya on crossed vajra, colours of faces, Vajravarahi, four dakinis with colours) tracks the source; 'lotus-like faces' for པདྨའི་ཞལ་བཞི is a defensible reading.

defects.detail: source is Marcellus IIII 41–62 on ulcers ('Radix peponis ... sanat ulcera', 'Carcinomata curantur coagulo leporis'); translation is about dandruff, lice and 'CHAPTER V ON CATARRHS OF THE HEAD'
none of the ulcer remedies 41–62 appear in the translation

reason: Translation is of a different passage (head lice and Chapter V catarrh remedies); the source's ulcer remedies are entirely absent.

defects.detail: source ends mid-word 'չեն բաւական լինել ի բնա-'; translation adds 'but need walls and roofs and other structures, likewise, by faith alone, without works, no one can build himself into a temple of God' — a doctrinal claim not on the page

reason: Blasphemy/curses passage and the 1 Cor 3 gold-silver-stubble image are faithful, but the final sentence is completed with an invented doctrinal conclusion.

defects.detail: invents headword 'Chong / Yuan Chong (profound and lofty)' and reads 李冲傳...冲器懷丨丨 and 王崇學業丨丨 as 'Yuan Chong'; the source has no such headword
drops the 石崇大雅吟 entry, the vertical 裴潛/貴無二…以矯虛…之弊 entry, and 何承天啟宋居士書…證譬堅明文詞 entry
garbled column order rendered as a clean three-headword dictionary page

reason: Only the 淵浩 and 淵曠 entries (Song shu, Qi shu, Wei shu Xu Zunming, Shen Yue) are rendered properly; a non-existent 'Yuan Chong' headword is invented and three entries are dropped.
